correctness.rationale: For the all-Hermitian Frobenius-normalized n-dimensional Fock truncation and M≥2n−1 equally spaced samples per circle, the angular DFT separates the diagonal radial n×n Vandermonde and two real copies of each (n−d)-column lag block. With fixed distinct offsets and strictly positive weights, Lagrange interpolation gives an operator-norm rank-one limit of ε^(n−1)A_0^(−1); its norm is exp(t)S_n(t)B(u,w). Smaller lag blocks have minimal singular values bounded below by c_d ε^(n−d−1), so cannot dominate the ε^(n−1) diagonal collapse. The largest singular value converges to exp(−t)H_n(t). The leading-coefficient Lagrange identity, monic Chebyshev bound and equality in weighted Cauchy–Schwarz prove B≥2^(n−2), uniquely at Lobatto offsets with endpoint-half weights, including n=2. Independent direct real-Hermitian sampling matrix SVDs for n=2,3,4 and shrinking ε corroborate both limiting constants; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The full-Hermitian tomographic information loss as measurement radii coalesce is a natural stability and sensor-design problem. The exact ε^(n−1) exponent and normalized coefficient, identification of the worst harmonic sector, and unique optimal radial offsets and budgets give useful experiment-design information not supplied merely by Chebyshev polynomial regression. The scope excludes nonlinear pure-state estimation, vanishing weights, finite-width optimality and photon-counting noise.
